_about: Pre/post concept test for Module 6 (molecular dynamics). 'answer' is the index of the correct option. Check the science before using with students.

questions.q: Why is MD used after docking?
options: To test whether the docked pose stays stable when atoms move
To find the structure of the protein
To measure binding in the lab
questions.why: Docking gives one rigid snapshot. MD adds motion over time.

questions.q: In an MD simulation the forces on each atom come from:
questions.why: A force field is a set of equations and parameters for bonds, angles and non-bonded interactions.

questions.q: What happens if the time step is too large?
options: The simulation becomes unstable and energy is not conserved
questions.why: Large steps miss the fastest motions, so errors build up and the simulation can explode.

questions.q: Why is a time step of about 2 fs used for proteins?
options: The fastest motions (bond vibrations) take about 10 fs
Proteins move only 2 fs at a time
It is the length of a nanosecond
questions.why: The step must be much shorter than the fastest vibration.

questions.q: Why are the first nanoseconds of a production run often discarded?
options: The system is still settling from its artificial starting state
The computer is slow at first
questions.why: Averages from before equilibration are biased by the starting conditions.

options: Minimise, then solvate and add ions
Solvate and add ions, minimise, equilibrate, then production run
questions.why: Each step prepares the system for the next one. Minimisation removes clashes before motion starts.

questions.q: What does a protein backbone RMSD that keeps rising during the whole run suggest?
options: The system has not reached a stable state
questions.why: A plateau means the structure fluctuates around a stable form. A steady climb means it is still changing.

options: How much each residue fluctuates around its average position
questions.why: RMSF is per residue. Loops and ends usually move more than helices and strands.

questions.q: The ligand RMSD rises to 8 Å and the drug is far from the pocket. What is the best conclusion?
options: The starting pose was not stable in this simulation
questions.why: The drug left the pocket in this run. You would check repeats and the pose before drawing strong conclusions.

questions.q: What does an MM-GBSA estimate give?
options: A rough end-point estimate useful for ranking, not an accurate binding energy
questions.why: MM-GBSA ignores some terms (for example entropy is often missing) and carries large errors.
